pergunta em ingles: What is the idea behind the chorus of the song “Cálice” by Chico Buarque?
alternativas em ingles: A) It is a religious song, a prayer in which the lyrical self asks God to free them from suffering. | B) The chorus criticizes alcohol consumption, since it talks about taking away the cup of wine. | C) The chorus uses the pun “cálice” (chalice) / “cale-se” (shut up) to denounce the censorship and violence of the military dictatorship, comparing that suffering to the martyrdom of Christ. | D) The lyrical self asks to be kept away from politics and prefers to stay silent to protect themselves.
contexto cultural: “Cálice” (1973) by Chico Buarque and Gilberto Gil was censored by the military regime. In Portuguese “cálice” (chalice) sounds like “cale-se” (“shut up”), so the line “Pai, afasta de mim esse cálice” (Father, take this cup away from me — Jesus in Gethsemane) is also a protest against censorship.
regiao subnacional: Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — songwriters' base; song known nationwide

pergunta em ingles: What is the origin of the Liberdade neighborhood in São Paulo?
alternativas em ingles: A) The neighborhood was founded in the early 20th century by Japanese immigrants, who turned an uninhabited area into the largest Asian enclave outside Asia. | B) The name “Liberdade” (Freedom) came about because Japanese immigrants, after leaving work on the coffee farms, sought a free and independent life in the area. | C) The area's origin is linked to the Black and enslaved population, with the Largo da Forca (Gallows Square) and the Cemitério dos Aflitos (Cemetery of the Afflicted), but this memory was erased over time by the strong presence of East Asian culture. | D) The neighborhood's identity has always been East Asian, since the first buildings in the area, such as temples and shops, were built by Chinese and Japanese people.
contexto cultural: Liberdade is known today as São Paulo's Japanese/East Asian district, but in the 18th–19th centuries it housed the city gallows (Largo da Forca) and the Cemitério dos Aflitos, the first public cemetery, where enslaved and poor people were buried. The Capela dos Aflitos remains as a trace of this Black history.
regiao subnacional: São Paulo (SP) — city of São Paulo

pergunta em ingles: What deadline does Municipal Law No. 4,985/2026 of Lavras give companies to remove wires that are not in use from utility poles, and what is the fine?
alternativas em ingles: A) 30 days from notification, with a daily fine of 1,000 | B) 90 days from publication, with a fine of 50 UFMs (Municipal Fiscal Units) per irregular pole | C) The law sets neither a deadline nor a fine amount; the deadline is defined in the notification and the fine is regulated by the executive branch | D) 60 days from notification, extendable for another 60, with the fine set by ANEEL (national electricity regulator)
contexto cultural: Lavras (MG) passed a local law on the 'fiação morta' problem: abandoned telecom cables hanging from electricity poles, a common urban issue in Brazilian cities. UFM = Unidade Fiscal do Município, a municipal index used to set fines.

pergunta em ingles: Who was the creator of cordel literature?
alternativas em ingles: A) There is no single creator; it is a collective popular culture | B) Leandro Gomes de Barros | C) Silvino Pirauá de Lima | D) João Martins de Athayde
contexto cultural: Cordel literature consists of popular rhymed booklets hung on strings ('cordéis') at Northeastern street markets, with roots in Iberian oral tradition. Leandro Gomes de Barros (PB) is called the 'father' of Brazilian printed cordel, and Silvino Pirauá was a pioneer, but the genre has no single creator.
observacao: Ambígua: muitos consideram Leandro Gomes de Barros o 'pai do cordel' (B). Corrigir grafia: 'Silvino Pirauá de Lima'.

pergunta em ingles: In which region of Brazil is Luiz Gonzaga's song “Asa Branca” set, and what context in the lyrics shows this?
alternativas em ingles: A) North, because it deals with migration to more populous regions | B) South, because it laments losses in cattle ranching | C) Northeast, because of the effects of drought | D) Center-West, because it mentions agriculture and cattle ranching
contexto cultural: “Asa Branca” (1947) by Luiz Gonzaga and Humberto Teixeira describes the drought of the Northeastern sertão: burnt land, dead cattle, and the farmer forced to leave, hoping to return when the rain comes back. The asa-branca (picazuro pigeon) leaving the sertão signals the drought.

pergunta em ingles: What is the reason behind the large number of churches in the city of Ouro Preto?
alternativas em ingles: A) Religious diversity among immigrants | B) The gold wealth and the lay brotherhoods (irmandades), with each social and racial group building its own church | C) An order from the Portuguese Crown to build one church per neighborhood | D) Competition among Jesuit missions
contexto cultural: In the 18th-century gold cycle, Vila Rica (Ouro Preto) became rich. Religious orders were banned from Minas, so lay brotherhoods (of white elites, free Black people, enslaved people, pardos) each built their own church — e.g., Santa Efigênia, Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Pretos and São Francisco de Assis (Aleijadinho).
